reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space of real dimension d>0, f differentiable everywhere, eta,beta,B>0,ell>=2, and the actual gradient globally beta-Lipschitz. For arbitrary x0,xp assume norm(x0-eta grad f(xp)-xp)<=sqrt(d eta) and 64 beta^2(ell d/B+ell^2)<=eta^(-2). Define h=x0-eta grad f(xp), q=N(h,eta I), P=N(0,eta I), nu=Lebesgue restricted to (0,1] product P. With theta=pi t/2 define Y=h+sin(theta)(x-h)+cos(theta)z and S=< (pi/2)(cos(theta)(x-h)-sin(theta)z), grad f(xp)-grad f(Y) >. Let m(x)=integral S dnu, mB(x)=integral min(B,max(-B,S)) dnu, V(x)=integral max(abs(S)-B,0) dnu, qhat=q.tilted(mB), and K=min(B^2/(40 beta^2 d eta^2),B/(8 beta eta)). Then m,mB,V are measurable, and every x satisfies V(x)>=0 and abs(m(x)-mB(x))<=V(x). The function exp(2ell V)-1 is Bochner integrable under q with integral<=2exp(-K), and under qhat with integral<=2exp(2B-K). The function exp(2ell abs(m-mB))-1 is Bochner integrable under qhat with integral<=2exp(2B-K).
